scope: Only the fixed independent C adapter, both exact checksum excerpts, identical decode-frame excerpts and their upstream manifest were read. No HIA product, finite matrix, compiler or native execution was invoked.

findings.detail: The adapter admits byte length 8 through 65536 inclusive, divisible by 8, order exactly 0 or 1, and non-null pointers. The caller must additionally retain readable n-byte storage and writable/aligned two-u32 output storage. The aligned local array has exact capacity 65536 bytes.

The adapter admits power-of-two page_size from 512 through 65536, n equal to page_size+24, order 0 or 1 and non-null pointers. The caller must retain all n readable bytes and aligned four-u32 output storage. aligned[16390] has 65560 bytes and frame+24 stays u32 aligned. The upper/lower checks short-circuit before the length calculation.

Call the C oracle only for a separately verified domain. Do not silently coerce bool, out-of-range values or malformed HIA control buffers through ctypes u32/int conversions and then label the result an original-domain C oracle. Record NOT_CALLED for cases outside the adapter's legitimate call domain.
On salt mismatch or zero pgno, walDecodeFrame returns before either checksum call. oracle_frame still writes all four outputs: input seed0, input seed1, page0, commit0.

When header and page checksum computation finishes but the stored checksum differs, return0 leaves the running checksum mutated to the computed values. oracle_frame writes both computed words and zero page/commit. Preserve these exact actual output bytes and return value. Compare with the HIA refusal semantics through a separately named projection; never overwrite the actual C seed with the input seed.

On return1, the adapter writes computed checksum words, decoded page number, and decoded commit/page-count word. Inputs stay copied into aligned locals; the wrapper should still retain actual before/after buffers.
Checksum implementations have the same unsigned32 algorithm and byte-order branches; the assert statements are regrouped in 3.53.2. Both decode-frame excerpts are byte-identical.
The executable decoder checks the first 8 header bytes and the page bytes. The upstream prose mentions first16; use executable code and preserve the manifest's explicit discrepancy.
